title: Poor safety features
text: Poor safety features. Yeah...no. Pressure cookers are generally safer than the ones our grandparents used, but this isn't like the brand name units today.  This thing scares me and I refuse to use it again.  There is no cancel option in the settings  - you have to unplug it to reset if it's programmed incorrectly. Additionally,  it will start cooking without the insert piece in the pot. Frankly, I prefer my fancy rice cooker and old school crockpot to this. The rice in this was sticky and clumpy. If you must have a pressure cooker, invest in a major name brand from a legitimate manufacturer.
